paras: The Keyport store riot was a Saturday-night attack in August 1885 in which a gang of men from the Big Woods chased a man into a store kept by Black people in Keyport, New Jersey, assaulted the proprietor and broke in the store front. The fight became a melee of brickbats, a thrown bottle and three shots from the store's side, and warrants were issued against the attackers.
According to the Keyport Enterprise, men from the Big Woods had visited the town on several Saturday nights, fighting, cursing, tearing down fences and destroying property.

Several of the gang attacked a man in front of the hotel, and he retreated into the store next door, with the gang following him. The store was "kept by colored people," who at once ordered the gang out. One of the men then went at the proprietor with a chair, and the proprietor threw a bottle that struck the man on the forehead and left "a terrible gash."

Once outside, the gang broke in the entire store front as brickbats flew. During the fight three shots were fired from the store's side, none of which struck anyone. No injury to the storekeepers is reported, and no one involved is named.

Several warrants had been issued by the time the Enterprise went to press, and the paper hoped the authorities would prosecute the offenders "to the end." Otherwise, it warned, a band would form to drive the Big Woods men out, as had been done years before. No report of arrests, a hearing or a trial was found.

The episode is known from one report: the Monmouth Inquirer of Freehold quoted the account in its county news column of 20 August 1885, crediting the previous week's Keyport Enterprise. The Enterprise cast the Big Woods men as "rowdies" and "loafers" and treated the affair as a disturbance of the peace, without assigning a racial motive. It nonetheless called the storekeepers "the darkies" and closed its account with the shots they fired.
No coverage in the Black press was found.

bases: A gang of rowdies pursued a man into a store kept by Black people, attacked the proprietor and wrecked the store front after being ordered out; the only account gives no racial motive and describes a two-sided melee rather than an attack on a Black community (A1).
The only report is the Keyport Enterprise's account as quoted by the Monmouth Inquirer (A1); no other paper was found.

accounts.label: Keyport Enterprise (local weekly), quoted by the Monmouth Inquirer
accounts.gist: Big Woods rowdies, who had disturbed Keyport for several Saturday nights, chased a man into a Black-kept store, assaulted the proprietor and broke in the store front in a melee of brickbats, bottle and three shots from the store's side; warrants were issued.

sources.note: County news column quoting the previous week's Keyport Enterprise: Big Woods gang chased a man into a store kept by colored people, assaulted the proprietor with a chair, broke in the store front; brickbats, three shots fired by 'the darkies'; warrants issued.
quotes: This store is kept by colored people and they at once ordered the gang out.
One of the Big Woodsers took a chair and made an assault on the proprietor, and the latter in turn threw a bottle which struck one of the gang on the forehead making a terrible gash.
After the Big Woodsers got outside they made a rush and broke in the entire store front. Brickbats flew thick and fast and there was a regular melee.
During the above racket three shots were fired by the darkies, but none took effect.
